set.body: Extend the item model beyond the fixed core (id/title/status/level/kind/milestone/priority) with a configurable optional-field set, so lightweight and heavyweight processes share one log. Config block (work_item_fields in .work/config.yml) enables fields per team; every enabled field carries a description so humans AND agents use it correctly; disabled fields never appear in prompts, forms, or validation. Recommended default-on: priority, estimate, risk, owner, milestone, acceptance_criteria, labels. Default-off: value, confidence, due_date, severity, time tracking. Dependencies stay typed (blocked_by/blocks, relates_to) and feed the Traceability Index. Design principles: small stable core; explicit documented options; conservative defaults; process-agnostic. Full spec discussed 2026-07-22; re-derive the detailed field table when this is planned.
set.title: Configurable work-item field model: optional fields (estimate, risk, effort, value, confidence, owner, due_date, acceptance_criteria, blocked_by/blocks) behind work_item_fields config

set.body: The release skill requires a hand-written '## X.Y.Z — unreleased' CHANGELOG section before a release can be cut, but nothing enforces writing it as features land — v0.13.0's section had to be manually reconstructed from 'git log v0.12.1..HEAD' after 36 commits piled up unlogged. Have the release skill (or a new 'worklog changelog-draft' step) generate a starting draft of the unreleased section from git log since the last tag, grouped by the existing commit-prefix convention (feat/fix/chore), excluding pure worklog housekeeping commits — a human/agent still reviews and edits the prose before stamping, but the 'we forgot to write it' failure mode goes away.
set.title: Auto-draft the release CHANGELOG unreleased section from git log

set.body: Reported alongside the duplicate-ticket bug: two assistant sessions ran in the same directory, one switched branches out from under the other mid-operation, and both independently 'fixed' the same problem in different ways. Nothing warns when work-log writes arrive from more than one process against the same directory. Add an advisory warning, and say in the generated policy that concurrent sessions belong in separate worktrees.
set.title: Concurrent sessions in one working directory corrupt each other's work

set.body: Sync reports counts — 'updated 2' — with no indication that a live ticket's title or state was replaced. In the reported incident that line would have caught the damage on the first run instead of the third. Naming the before and after for each overwritten field costs one extra read per updated ticket, which is a real cost worth measuring before committing to it.
set.title: Sync should say which ticket fields it is about to overwrite

set.body: When a union merge resurrects events a compaction removed, the pre-commit merge guard blocks the merge commit and prints: 'Run: python3 bin/compact.py .work/todo.jsonl .work/done.jsonl to recompact.' That remedy cannot be followed. compact.py refuses to run while the logs have uncommitted changes ('compaction must be its own commit, spec 7') -- and the blocked merge IS the uncommitted change. The guard prevents the commit that compaction requires, so the only ways out are --no-verify or git merge --abort, neither of which the message mentions. Hit live on 2026-07-31 when the nightly compaction landed on main while a PR was in CI. The working resolution is to abort the merge, restore the logs from the compacted branch, and re-apply the branch's own events on top of the compacted base -- same fold, far fewer lines. Either teach compact.py to accept a merge-in-progress, or change the guard's message to print the resolution that actually works.
set.title: Merge guard's printed remedy cannot be run from the state it creates

set.body: What is left of the IA content model after Phase 5's gate promotion shipped. The phase-5 ticket bundled three unrelated things: promoting the CI gates to hard failures (done, and the item on the design docs' extension roadmap), a rendering port to other wiki platforms, and a document-search command. Only the first had a user. This epic holds the rest so the parent epic can close on the value that actually shipped rather than being held open by work nobody has planned. Deliberately NOT filed here: one item per wiki platform (GitLab, Azure DevOps, Confluence). The config names github-wiki and no one has asked for another; those get filed when a platform has a user, not before. Also dropped: the glossary page, which its own plan marks optional.
set.title: IA reader plane: platform-portable rendering and document search

set.body: The renderer never reads the wiki system from config. Page naming and cross-page links are written for Gollum, the GitHub wiki engine: roughly forty wikilink sites and five naming helpers assume its conventions. Porting to any other platform today means editing all of them. Introduce one seam -- a small interface for page naming and link syntax -- so a second platform is a new implementation rather than a rewrite. Doing the seam without a second platform is only worth it if it stays small: if it grows past a naming/link interface, stop and wait for a real second consumer.
set.title: Extract a render adapter seam so page naming is not hardcoded to Gollum

set.body: There is no way to search the content model from the command line -- no find, no search. Everything the answer needs is already generated and on disk in the inventory and the graph: every document with its type and truth state, every typed edge between documents, items, tickets and PRs. A read-only command over those two files would answer 'which plan decided this?' and 'what is superseded?' without a network call or a new index.
set.title: worklog find: search the generated inventory and graph from the CLI

set.resolution: New 'worklog changelog-draft' generates the unreleased section from git log since the last tag, grouped by commit type, excluding commits that touch only the log and generated files. Markdown on stdout so it pipes; excluded commits reported on stderr so nothing vanishes silently. Version is never guessed — the semver bump stays a human call. Release skill documents it as a starting point, not the notes.

set.body: The fold drops any event whose id sorts at or below a compaction watermark, on the assumption that the compaction already folded it into a snapshot. That assumption only holds for events the compaction actually saw. An event created on a branch before the compaction ran on main was never folded into any snapshot, yet it sorts below the watermark, so merging the branch back makes the fold discard it and the work vanishes with no error. Reproduced deterministically: an item created on a branch disappears entirely after the merge. This is the real reason the merge guard must keep blocking, and it is why recompacting during a blocked merge is unsafe -- the recompaction would verify successfully against a fold that has already discarded the branch's events, making the loss permanent. The guard currently catches every instance, so nothing is lost today, but the underlying watermark rule is unsound and fixing it properly changes how compaction records what it folded.
set.title: Compaction watermark can silently drop branch-local events the snapshot never folded

set.resolution: Guard now names the real risk (the fold drops these on read) and points at worklog merge-rescue, which performs ADR-0005's manual resolution: keep the compacted side, re-emit this branch's own events above the watermark, verify nothing vanished. Recompaction was rejected as a remedy — it would verify against an already-lossy fold. ADR-0006 corrects ADR-0005's hygiene classification.

Sync now names every live ticket field it replaced, before -> after, in its own report block above drift, and in --dry-run while it is still hypothetical. The cost the ticket flagged is avoided: one batched 'pull --keys' per RUN rather than a read per ticket, using a verb the adapter contract already had, and the run prints how many tickets it read and how long that took.

Advisory warning when two sessions are live in one working directory, plus the worktree rule in the generated policy. Session identity comes from the harness (hook session_id) because the CLI is short-lived and has no stable pid/ppid/sid. SessionEnd prunes so a finished session stops warning the next one.

Optional fields now live in a catalog (bin/item_fields.py) with per-field descriptions, enabled per team via work_item_fields in .work/config.yml. A disabled field has no flag at all — invisible rather than rejected, which is what 'never appears in prompts' means for a CLI whose --help is the prompt. The core stays fixed and unconfigurable because priority/depends_on are load-bearing for the roadmap. estimate moved from two hardcoded flags into the catalog. Field table derived in docs/plans/2026-08-01-configurable-item-fields.md, as the item asked.

One seam in bin/wiki_flavor.py: link() and sanitize(), nothing else. [[Page]] is now the renderer's CANONICAL notation, translated once at the output boundary (render_all + banner), so all ~44 prose link sites stayed exactly as written and a second platform is a new class rather than 44 edits. Gollum output verified byte-identical across 319 rendered files. The renderer now reads wiki.system from config, which it never did. A test-only second flavor proves the seam; no speculative platform ships, and a test fails if the interface grows past two methods.

worklog find reads the generated graph: text/type/truth-state search, a node's edges in both directions (--links), and every edge of one type (--edge). Answers the ticket's two questions directly — 'which plan decided this' is an inbound edge, 'what is superseded' is --edge supersedes or --truth superseded. Read-only, no network, no new index; lives in ia_graph.py which already owned the graph and its adjacency.

Both children shipped: #271 (render adapter seam, PR #282) and #272 (worklog find, PR #281). The epic held what was left of the phase-5 bundle after the gate promotion; per its own body, per-platform wiki items are NOT filed here — they get filed when a platform has a user.

set.body: The commit-msg hook exempts merge commits from its item-reference rule, and the pre-commit hook only syntax-checks the event log and bin/ -- it never looks at tests/ or the plugin scripts. A merge that leaves conflict markers in those files therefore commits cleanly, and the damage is only found when someone runs the test suite. Hit twice while merging main into feature branches: markers survived in tests/test_plugin.py and in the plugin install/uninstall scripts. The fix is cheap and belongs in pre-commit, which already reads every staged file: refuse any staged text file containing a conflict marker, with no merge exemption, because a merge commit is exactly when this happens.
set.title: Conflict markers can reach a commit: the merge exemption plus unparsed tests

set.body: Two agents working in different worktrees or branches mint event ids from the same clock and pure randomness, so ids created in the same millisecond sort arbitrarily and carry nothing about where they came from. Replace five characters of a locally-generated ULID's entropy with the short git commit hash, keeping the 26-character format and the time prefix intact, so events from different branches are distinguishable and traceable at a glance. The deterministic ingest id is deliberately excluded: it must stay byte-identical across machines for the same remote change, and a per-clone git hash would break that.
set.title: Stamp generated ULIDs with the short git hash so concurrent branches diverge

set.resolution: Compaction now records a per-item 'through' on each snapshot, the fold drops per item (an item with no snapshot never loses events), and a snapshot sorts at its through rather than its mint time so a branch's later close applies on top instead of being erased. ADR-0007. Legacy logs fold unchanged.
pre-commit refuses any staged file containing a conflict marker, with no merge exemption — a merge is exactly when this happens.

Locally-minted ULIDs carry the 5-char short git hash in place of 5 chars of entropy; 26-char format, time prefix and sort order unchanged. deterministic() deliberately excluded so ingest ids stay byte-identical across clones.

set.body: Stamp the changelog with upgrade guidance for repos on older versions, snapshot the roadmap, bump the version lockstep, tag, and publish. Covers the eight tickets closed in this wave plus the per-item compaction watermark fix.
set.title: Cut release v0.19.0

set.body: Every command that names an existing item resolves a full ULID or an unambiguous prefix through one helper, except the sidecar writers. Passing a short id to link-pr writes docs/.index/item/<prefix>.yml instead of the real item's sidecar, so the PR edge never reaches the graph and the release evidence gate still reports the item as unlinked -- with no error, because the write succeeded. This is the same class already fixed for close and update, which used to mint phantom orphan items from the short ids that list and show print.
set.title: link-pr and pr-sync accept an id prefix and write a phantom sidecar

set.resolution: link-pr now resolves the id through _resolve before writing, so a prefix files the real item's sidecar instead of a phantom. Eleven phantom sidecars from this release's own linking removed.

v0.19.0 tagged at 994a28a and released on GitHub with upgrade guidance for 0.18.0-and-earlier installations. Version lockstep bumped across manifest, CLI, README and 26 skill files; roadmap snapshotted and indexed.

set.body: v0.19.0 stamped the short git hash into locally-minted ULIDs by overwriting five characters of entropy. That was the wrong trade: an id is issued once and must never collide, so spending entropy to carry provenance weakens the one guarantee the id exists to provide. Restore the full 80 bits and record the originating git commit as a separate property on every event instead, which also traces better -- an item's ULID is minted once, so it could only ever name the branch the item was created on, while a per-event field names the origin of every event.
set.title: Restore full ULID entropy; record git provenance as its own event field

set.resolution: ULIDs are back to full 80-bit entropy; the git short sha now rides on every event as its own 'git' field. Provenance is per-event rather than baked into an id that is minted once, so a later update names the commit it was actually authored at.

set.body: Corrective patch release: restore full ULID entropy and move git provenance onto the event as its own field.
set.title: Cut release v0.19.1

set.resolution: v0.19.1 tagged and released with full ULID entropy restored and per-event git provenance.
